description: Canonical evidence inventory for the AgentDojo live evaluation and the offline control experiments. Lists every artifact a paper or spec claim rests on, so the claim stays auditable from version control alone. This file records an index, not a measurement: it must never be read as evidence in place of the artifact it points at.
hash_encoding: sha256 and size are over LF-normalised content (what Git stores), so a core.autocrlf=true checkout does not invalidate them
indexed_granularity: One entry per top-level run artifact (manifest.json, index.jsonl, report.json, sidecar.jsonl, derived attribution files). Per-cell substance -- the agentshield-*/ trajectory logs and the new sidecar/ per-cell gate artifacts -- is committed next to those files but not hashed individually here, so the index stays small enough to review; a cell's outcome is also on its index.jsonl row. Frozen directories from the 120B pair are indexed under this same rule. The one exception is the paired 120B arms' per-cell workspaces, which the latency derivation reads: they are pinned collectively by live_latency_derived.json, whose every row carries its source file's LF-normalised digest and whose source_digest_set_sha256 covers all 160 of them. Files under benchmark/results/ that are not entries here -- earlier generations of a comparison, the raw outputs of the experiment driver, and runs the paper does not report -- are enumerated under the not_indexed key, so their presence in the repository is explained rather than unexplained. None of them is shipped in the anonymous snapshot; the only file in that group the snapshot carries is this inventory.

known_gaps.what_it_means: The 120B governed report's gate statistics describe only the 3 cells of the run's final invocation, because the pre-per-cell sidecar was truncated at the top of every invocation and cached cells wrote no rows. The field is not wrong about what it counted; it is easy to misread as covering the arm. Per-cell coverage for the paired 80-cell comparison is in attribution.json next to it (57 of 80 mapped).
known_gaps.remedy_applied_for_future_runs: one sidecar artifact per cell, keyed by cell identity, written atomically (harness change; gate_source_sha256 moved, so these directories are no longer resumable under their run-tags)

known_gaps.observed: 9 solvable in the 2026-09-27 arm, 8 in the 2026-09-29 arm; difference is injection_task_10 alone
known_gaps.what_it_means: The two arms measured their own validity legs two days apart at temperature 0 and disagreed on one task, so every Step 9 number is computed on the 80-cell intersection of the two frozen sets rather than on either directory's own denominator.
known_gaps.remedy_applied_for_future_runs: --validity-only writes one shared validity_freeze.json whose sha256 every arm must cite; the freeze is in CACHE_COMPARED_KEYS and a mismatch fails closed (exit 6)

known_gaps.what_it_means: 6 of the 15 security flips occurred in cells where the gate actually intervened, 3 have blocked_calls=0 and 6 (all user_task_28) are unmapped. Occurrence is not proof of cause, which is the wording the spec already uses.
known_gaps.remedy_applied_for_future_runs: per-cell sidecar artifacts remove the truncation, so the confirmatory replication reports attribution at full coverage

not_indexed.reason: The inventory cannot index itself. It is the only file of this group that the anonymous snapshot ships.

An earlier generation of the auxiliary SCI-600 comparison. It scores the same 600-case, three-label fixture under a different metric definition and with a different baseline naming, so the content-keyword baseline reads 0.3177 Macro-F1 here against 0.487 in the frozen report and the AgentShield rung is called 'chain-aware' where the frozen report calls it 'production'. No number in the paper rests on these files. The _v2 pair repeats the v1 pair with only the recorded dataset string changed -- one generation names the dataset through the container's workspace root, the other through the repository checkout -- and the table pair additionally differs in its runtime column, which moves with the machine. Both generations record a host-specific absolute path, so neither is shipped.

The same driver run against a semi-real fixture of 150 cases, kept in two generations that differ only in the recorded dataset path string. The paper describes neither this fixture nor a semi-real comparison, so nothing here is quoted; the files are the derivation trail of a fixture that was not promoted into the paper.

The raw per-experiment outputs of the offline experiment driver, concatenated by full_paper_report.json. main_comparison.json and ablation.json restate the SCI-600 fixture and review_cost.json repeats its table under a cost model, but they are earlier snapshots of it: the production configuration reads 0.4349 Macro-F1 there against 0.4298 in the frozen report, which is why the paper quotes the frozen report and says 'approximately 0.43' instead of either number exactly. robustness.json scores four hand-built adversarial cases, latency.json is an in-process micro-benchmark over 1000 iterations with sub-millisecond percentiles, and case_studies.json walks four attack chains. The paper reports none of the three, and its latency section comes from the trace replay indexed as agentdojo_native_trace_replay.json.

Runs whose endpoints the paper does not report, so no claim needs them. trajectory_eval.json is an early sweep over a 2000-sample stratified subset of the AgentDojo dump (1961 attack, 39 benign) reconstructed from attack metadata rather than recorded, and it is not the paired counterfactual comparison that paired_trajectory_eval.json indexes. native_trace_eval.json is the dump-wide version of the trace replay the paper does describe: it counts 13,574 attack steps where the indexed agentdojo_native_trace_replay.json counts the 442 in the 400 sampled trajectories, and everything else it shares with the indexed file agrees, so it is a superset rather than a contradiction. live_agent_governance.json is a governance-ladder run on a simulated backend over 8 tasks and 53 tools that measures no endpoint (asr_measured, utility_measured and task_success_measured are all false, and official_agentdojo_benchmark is false), so nothing in the paper could rest on it; it also names the model endpoint it called, which is a further reason it is not shipped.
